verdict.rationale: The Solo 2 firmware source is public on GitHub with build instructions (cargo build, flashing to an EVK), Hacker keys can be flashed with self-built firmware, and a community member confirms it is open source firmware. However, nothing shows that a standard retail key's signed vendor firmware can be verified against that source, so the 'don't take the vendor's word for what runs on the device' part is only partly covered. missing for 10: reproducible builds or a documented way to verify the firmware on a retail key against the source, any independent security audit, an explicit open-source license statement for the firmware.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the firmware is open source or independently audited, so I don't have to take the vendor's word for what runs on the device

citations.quote: So it's open source firmware, not open source hardware.
On a **Hacker** key you can build and flash your own firmware.
Flash your own firmware, experiment with new features, and learn how a security key works end to end.
